instructions:
1. Set up on the 45 degree bench with your feet in the footrests and one thigh against the pad.
2. Place one hand behind your head and the other on your waist.
3. Bend your knee and bring your opposite elbow toward it, twisting your torso.
4. Return to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist from your core, not your neck.
2. Keep your hips pressed into the pad.
3. Move slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Set your feet in the footrests and press your thighs against the pad.
2. Cross your arms over your chest and bend forward at the hips.
3. Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line.
4. Lower under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stop at a straight line; do not overextend the lower back.
2. Drive the movement with your glutes and lower back.
3. Keep your neck neutral.
4. Move slowly, no swinging.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and arms overhead.
2. Lift your upper back and reach your arms forward toward your heels.
3. Hold briefly.
4. Lower under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your lower back into the floor.
2. Lift with your abs, not your neck.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands in fists.
2. Raise one knee while punching the opposite arm overhead.
3. Lower and switch sides, raising the other knee and punching the other arm.
4. Keep a steady rhythm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight for balance.
2. Drive your knee up to hip height.
3. Exhale as you punch.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Extend your right arm and left leg until level with your body.
3. Hold briefly, then return to the plank.
4. Extend your left arm and right leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square; do not let them rotate.
2. Brace your core so your hips do not sag.
3. Move slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Extend your right arm and left leg level with your body.
3. Hold.
4. Return to the plank, then extend your left arm and right leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep your hips level.
2. Do not let your hips rotate or sag.
3. Breathe steadily through the hold.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Extend your right arm and left leg, then return to the plank and pause.
3. Extend your left arm and right leg, then return and pause.
4. Keep the pauses controlled. Repeat.
tips:
1. Reset your core brace during each pause.
2. Keep your hips square throughout.
3. Move slowly, no rushing.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward.
2. Keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the right dumbbell to your shoulder.
3. Lower under control.
4. Curl the left dumbbell. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not swing; keep your upper arms still.
2. Fully extend at the bottom of each rep.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend one knee and slide the other leg out to the side, reaching down to touch that heel.
3. Push back to standing.
4. Repeat on the other side. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your bent knee in line with your toes.
2. Keep your chest up and core braced.
3. Push through the heel of the bent leg.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
3. Reach your right hand toward your right heel, then return to center.
4. Reach your left hand toward your left heel. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders off the floor throughout.
2. Crunch to the side using your obliques.
3. Move under control.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Lift your right leg straight back without arching your lower back.
3. Hold briefly, then lower.
4. Lift your left leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute of the lifting leg.
2. Keep your hips level and core braced.
3. Do not let your lower back sag.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with arms extended in front and legs straight back.
2. Lift your right arm and left leg off the floor.
3. Hold briefly, then lower.
4. Lift your left arm and right leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your lower back and glutes.
2. Keep your neck neutral, eyes down.
3. Raise your arm and leg to the same height.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of the band, holding a handle in each hand, palms facing in.
2. Keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the right handle to your shoulder.
3. Lower under control.
4. Curl the left handle. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral grip throughout.
2. Do not swing; keep your upper arms still.
3. Control the band on the way down.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing in.
2. Keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the right dumbbell to your shoulder.
3. Lower under control.
4. Curl the left dumbbell. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral grip throughout.
2. Do not swing the weights.
3. Keep your upper arms still.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Shift your weight onto your left leg and curl your right heel toward your glutes.
3. Squeeze the hamstring, then lower under control.
4. Repeat with the left leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Bring the heel as close to the glutes as possible.
2. Keep your knees aligned and hips still.
3. Move slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
2. Step your right foot up beside your right hand into a lunge.
3. Rotate your torso right and reach your right arm to the ceiling.
4. Return your hand and foot to the plank.
5. Repeat on the left side. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee over your ankle.
2. Brace your core during the rotation.
3. Move under control.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and hands lightly behind your head.
2. Lift your shoulders and twist to bring your right elbow toward your left knee.
3. Lower under control.
4. Twist to bring your left elbow toward your right knee. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist using your obliques, not your arms.
2. Do not pull on your neck.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
2. Step your right foot up outside your right hand into a low lunge.
3. Return your right foot to the plank.
4. Step your left foot outside your left hand, then return. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee over your ankle.
2. Keep your core braced and hips level.
3. Move under control.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and arms by your sides.
2. Lift your right leg and left arm toward each other, reaching for your toe.
3. Lower under control.
4. Lift your left leg and right arm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working leg straight.
2. Press your lower back into the floor.
3. Lift with your abs.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with your hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Pull up while shifting toward your right hand, keeping the left arm straight.
3. Lower under control.
4. Pull up shifting toward your left hand. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbow down to lead with the back.
2. Keep the straight arm extended along the bar.
3. Lower fully under control.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended forward.
2. Step your left leg back into a lunge while drawing your elbow back like an archer.
3. Push through your front foot to return to standing.
4. Repeat stepping back with the right leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee over your ankle.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
3. Control the descent.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended out to your sides.
2. Make small forward circles with both arms.
3. Gradually increase the size of the circles.
4. Keep the motion smooth. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight at shoulder height.
2. Keep your core braced and posture tall.
3. Move smoothly and under control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended out to your sides.
2. Make small backward circles with both arms.
3. Gradually increase the size of the circles.
4. Keep the motion smooth. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight at shoulder height.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades as you circle back.
3. Move smoothly and under control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms out to your sides at shoulder height.
2. Bring your arms forward and cross them in front of your chest.
3. Open your arms back out to the sides.
4. Keep a steady rhythm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms at shoulder height.
2. Squeeze your chest as you cross.
3. Exhale as you cross, inhale as you open.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
2. Bring your arms forward and cross them in front of your chest.
3. Open your arms back out and press your chest forward, squeezing your shoulder blades.
4. Keep a steady rhythm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as you cross and your back as you open.
2. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
3. Exhale as you cross, inhale as you open.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Swing both arms forward and cross them in front of your chest.
3. Open the arms wide, then cross them again, alternating which arm passes on top.
4. Return your arms out to the sides to the starting position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
2. Alternate which arm crosses on top each rep for balanced work.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso still.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees with your forearms in front of you.
3. Brace your upper arms and pulse them forward and back in small movements.
4. Keep the pulses short and steady.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the pulses small and controlled.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
3. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your neck loose.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bring your forearms in front of you, palms facing the floor, elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
3. Pulse your hands toward each other so one passes over the other.
4. Return to the start, alternating which hand crosses on top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the crossing movement small and controlled.
2. Alternate the top hand each rep for balanced work.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso still.
4. Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Turn your palms to face the floor.
3. Pulse your arms up and down in small, quick movements.
4. Keep your arms at shoulder height throughout.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the pulses small to stay at shoulder height.
2. Brace your core for stability.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Hold a steady pace and breathe evenly.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Turn your palms to face the ceiling.
3. Pulse your arms up and down in small, quick movements.
4. Keep your arms at shoulder height throughout.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the pulses small to stay at shoulder height.
2. Brace your core for stability.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Hold a steady pace and breathe evenly.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Make fists and hold your hands near your chest.
3. Lift your right knee and rotate your torso to the left.
4. Lower the knee and return your torso to center.
5. Lift your left knee and rotate your torso to the right.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the knee high to fully flex the hip.
2. Start the rotation from your obliques, not your arms.
3. Keep a steady pace so both sides work evenly.
4. Exhale as you lift and twist.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms forward.
3. Swing both arms forward until they cross in front of your chest.
4. Swing your arms back out to the sides.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms at shoulder height throughout.
2. Move smoothly and under control.
3. Brace your core to stay stable.
4. Open the chest fully on the backswing.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bring both arms behind your back.
3. Hold your forearms parallel to the floor, crossing one over the other.
4. Hold the stretch and feel it across the front of your shoulders.
5. Release and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
2. Apply gentle pressure to deepen the stretch slowly.
3. Keep your chest open and posture tall.
4. Breathe steadily and do not force the range.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your right arm straight overhead and keep your left arm down at your side.
3. Lower your right arm while raising your left arm overhead, keeping both arms straight.
4. Continue alternating arms up and down in a steady rhythm.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both arms straight through the full range.
2. Move smoothly to build coordination.
3. Inhale as one arm rises, exhale as it lowers.
4. Reach long through your fingertips.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of a resistance band.
2. Hold the handles in front of your chest with arms bent and palms facing you.
3. Press the handles up while rotating your palms to face forward.
4. Extend your arms fully overhead.
5. Reverse the motion back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
2. Pick a band tension that lets you keep good form.
3. Keep your wrists neutral and stacked.
4. Brace your core to stay upright while standing.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing you, elbows in front of your torso.
2. Press the dumbbells up and rotate your palms to face forward as you lift.
3. Extend your arms fully overhead.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly, rotating your palms back toward you to return to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate the wrists smoothly through the whole press, not just at the top.
2. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your back against the pad to avoid arching.
4. Pick a weight that lets you control the rotation.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine. Grasp the handles with a reverse grip, palms facing you, shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull your body up until your chin passes the bar.
3. Squeeze your back at the top.
4. Lower your body slowly until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down and back, not out to the sides.
2. Set the assistance so you can control both the lift and the descent.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine. Grasp the handles with a reverse grip, palms facing you, hands close together.
2. Pull your body up until your chin passes the bar.
3. Squeeze your back at the top.
4. Lower your body slowly until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso through the pull.
2. Set the assistance so you can control both the lift and the descent.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine. Grasp the handles with a reverse grip, palms facing you, wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull your body up until your chin passes the bar.
3. Squeeze your back at the top.
4. Lower your body slowly until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows and pull your shoulder blades down.
2. Set the assistance so you can control both the lift and the descent.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing away, hands close together.
2. Pull your body up until your chin passes the bar.
3. Squeeze your back at the top.
4. Lower your body slowly until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down toward your hips as you pull.
2. Set the assistance so you can control both the lift and the descent.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Kneel or stand on the assist pad of the machine and grip the handles with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with your arms fully extended and your shoulders engaged.
3. Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower your body under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down and back toward your hips to lead with the lats.
2. Set the assistance so you can complete clean reps with full range.
3. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your core braced to stop your body from swinging.

instructions:
1. Kneel or stand on the assist pad of the machine and grip the handles with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with your arms fully extended and your shoulders engaged.
3. Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower your body under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull your elbows down toward your sides to target the outer lats.
2. Set the assistance so you can complete clean reps with full range.
3. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your chest up and avoid shrugging your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Have a partner hold your feet down for stability.
3. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands by your ears.
4. Curl your upper body up toward your knees.
5. Lower your upper body back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you sit up and inhale as you lower.
2. Move with control instead of using momentum.
3. Do not pull on your neck with your hands.
4. Keep your lower back rounding off the floor as you rise.

instructions:
1. Stand next to a wall or sturdy support and hold it for balance.
2. Keep your torso upright and your supporting leg slightly bent.
3. Swing your right leg forward and backward in a smooth, controlled motion.
4. Complete your swings, then switch to your left leg.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the swings controlled and avoid throwing the leg with momentum.
2. Stay tall and do not lean forward or back.
3. Increase the range gradually as the hip loosens.
4. Keep your core engaged to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with your back straight.
2. Raise your right arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your back.
3. Use your left hand to gently pull the right elbow toward your head.
4. Hold the stretch.
5. Switch arms and repeat.
tips:
1. Pull gently; the stretch should feel mild, not painful.
2. Keep your core engaged to stay upright.
3. Breathe slowly and deeply to relax into the stretch.
4. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.

instructions:
1. Sit in the machine and secure your feet on the footrests.
2. Press your upper back against the pad and cross your arms over your chest.
3. Push back and extend your spine until your torso forms a straight line.
4. Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your lower back.
5. Lower under control to the start position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and controlled in both directions.
2. Stop at a straight line and do not hyperextend the spine.
3. Brace your core to support the spine.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand facing an incline bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Lean forward and place both arms over the bench, palms down and arms straight.
3. Let your chest sink toward the bench until you feel a stretch across the chest and shoulders.
4. Hold the position and breathe steadily.
5. Release and return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
2. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
3. Breathe deeply to deepen the stretch.
4. Increase the stretch gradually, never forcing it.

instructions:
1. Sit on a box with feet flat and arms extended straight in front at shoulder height.
2. Pull your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
3. Open your chest at the end of the movement.
4. Extend your arms back to the front.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the shoulder blades together without shrugging.
2. Keep your core engaged and torso upright.
3. Move in a slow, controlled rhythm.
4. Exhale as you retract, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand facing an incline bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge forward and place your hands on the bench with arms straight and back flat.
3. Push your hips back until you feel a stretch in your back and hamstrings.
4. Return your hips toward the start position.
5. Move in and out of the stretch in a controlled rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat throughout the movement.
2. Drive the stretch from your hips, not by rounding the waist.
3. Use smooth, controlled motion with no jerking.
4. Keep a slight bend in the knees if hamstrings are tight.

instructions:
1. Stand near an incline bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Lean forward and place your hands on the bench with arms straight.
3. Push your hips back and lower your chest toward the floor.
4. Feel the stretch along your back and hold the position.
5. Release and return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and arms straight.
2. Brace your core to protect the lower back.
3. Keep shoulders relaxed and away from the ears.
4. Plant your feet firmly for a stable base.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat with shins flat on the floor and knees about hip-width apart.
2. Keep your back straight and place your hands on your thighs.
3. Lean backward slowly and reach your hands toward your heels.
4. Push your hips forward to lengthen the front of your torso.
5. Hold, then return upright.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Only lean as far as is comfortable for your flexibility.
2. Keep your hips pushed forward to deepen the stretch through the abs.
3. Breathe slowly and steadily to help the muscles relax.
4. Stop if you feel any pinching in your lower back.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at chest height to a sturdy point.
2. Stand side-on to the anchor and grip the band with both hands at your chest.
3. Step out to create tension and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
4. Brace your core and press the band straight out in front of your chest.
5. Resist the pull that tries to rotate your torso and hold for a few seconds.
6. Bring your hands back to your chest with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and shoulders square; do not let the band twist you.
2. Brace your core before each press.
3. Press the band straight out, level with your chest.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band low behind your head.
2. Lie on a bench or the floor with your head near the anchor.
3. Grip the band with both hands and extend your arms toward the ceiling.
4. Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower your hands toward your forehead.
5. Extend your elbows to press your hands back up against the band tension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move at the elbows.
2. Control the band on the way down; do not let it snap back.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your rib cage down to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with a wide overhand grip.
2. Keep your chest up and shoulders set back.
3. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
4. Squeeze at the top and hold briefly.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift straight up and down; do not roll your shoulders.
2. Keep your arms straight so the traps do the work.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a weight you can control through a full squeeze.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your upper back behind your neck.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Bend your knees slightly to load your legs.
4. Drive through your heels and press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the bar back behind your neck with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use leg drive to start the press, then finish with your arms.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso upright.
3. Exhale forcefully as you press up.
4. Only use this movement if you have good shoulder mobility.

instructions:
1. Set a decline bench and lie back with your feet secured under the foot pads.
2. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it with arms extended.
3. Lower the barbell slowly to your lower chest, keeping control.
4. Press the barbell back up until your arms are fully extended.
5. Rack the barbell when finished.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet locked under the pads to stay stable.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso tight.
3. Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
4. Use a spotter when training heavy on a decline.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it with arms extended.
3. Lower the barbell slowly to your upper chest, keeping control.
4. Press the barbell back up until your arms are fully extended.
5. Rack the barbell when finished.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and drive them into the floor for stability.
2. Brace your core and keep your shoulder blades pulled back.
3. Lower the bar to your upper chest under control.
4. Avoid setting the incline too steep, as it shifts work to the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Set a bench behind you and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell across your upper back.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and keep your chest up.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until you sit on the bench.
4. Pause briefly without relaxing, then drive through your heels to stand up fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
2. Keep your chest up and spine neutral throughout.
3. Sit back onto the bench, do not drop down hard.
4. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your back straight and your gaze down and forward.
4. Pull the barbell to your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the barbell under control until your arms are extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and spine neutral to avoid rounding.
2. Drive your elbows back and up, not flaring wide.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip about shoulder-width.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your back straight and your gaze down and forward.
4. Pull the barbell to your lower abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body.
5. Lower the barbell under control until your arms are extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and spine neutral to avoid rounding.
2. Drive your elbows straight back along your sides.
3. The underhand grip lets the biceps assist, so keep the wrists firm.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a supinated grip narrower than shoulder-width.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your core braced.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows fixed in place.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move at a controlled pace and avoid swinging the bar with momentum.
2. Keep your back straight and shoulders set throughout.
3. The close grip emphasizes the long head, so focus on the squeeze.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a supinated grip about shoulder-width.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your core braced.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows fixed in place.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move at a controlled pace and avoid swinging the bar with momentum.
2. Keep your back straight and shoulders set throughout.
3. Keep your wrists neutral, not bent back.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a supinated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your core braced.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows fixed in place.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move at a controlled pace and avoid swinging the bar with momentum.
2. Keep your back straight and shoulders set throughout.
3. The wide grip emphasizes the short head for arm width.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a supinated grip about shoulder-width.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your core braced.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows fixed in place.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move at a controlled pace and avoid swinging the bar with momentum.
2. Keep your back straight and shoulders set throughout.
3. Keep your wrists neutral, not bent back.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench with a barbell across your upper back, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Rest the top of your rear foot on the bench.
3. Keep your chest up and spine neutral.
4. Bend your front knee and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
5. Drive through your front heel to stand back up, fully extending the hip and knee.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Lower under control to keep tension on the working leg.
3. Brace your core to resist trunk rotation on the single leg.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench with a barbell resting across your upper back. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Place the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
3. Keep your chest up and spine neutral. Bend your right knee and lower until your left knee nearly touches the floor.
4. Push through your right heel to stand back up, extending the hip and knee.
5. Finish the set, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Lower with control to keep tension on the working leg.
3. Lean the torso slightly forward to bias the glutes.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell on the floor, gripping it overhand.
2. Explosively extend your hips and knees, shrug, and pull the bar to your shoulders with elbows pointing forward.
3. Dip your knees slightly, then drive the bar overhead by extending your legs and arms.
4. As the bar rises, step one foot forward and the other back into a split squat, lowering until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
5. Push through your front heel to stand, bring your feet together, then lower the bar to the floor. Repeat, alternating the lead leg.
tips:
1. Drive with the legs to generate power for the bar.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes in the split.
3. Keep the chest up and spine neutral throughout.
4. Brace your core hard before pressing overhead.

instructions:
1. Squat down with feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell overhand on the floor in front of you.
2. Explosively extend your hips and knees, shrug, and pull the bar to your shoulders with elbows forward.
3. Brace your core and press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control.
5. Reverse the clean to return the bar to the floor. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive from the legs to start the clean.
2. Keep a firm grip and let the wrists rotate as the bar reaches the shoulders.
3. Exhale as you press the bar overhead.
4. Keep the bar path close to your body.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell closer than shoulder-width.
2. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms extended.
3. Lower the bar with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
4. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended, driving with your triceps and chest.
5. Rack the bar safely. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked to load the triceps.
2. Move with control rather than bouncing the bar.
3. Keep your feet planted for a stable base.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell closer than shoulder-width, arms extended over your chest.
2. Lower the bar with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
3. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended, driving with your triceps.
4. Rack the bar safely. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked to bias the triceps.
2. Move with control rather than using momentum.
3. Keep your feet planted for stability.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
2. Step your right foot back and across behind your left leg.
3. Lower your hips until your left thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your left heel to return to standing.
5. Alternate sides each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Stay upright with your chest lifted and core braced.
3. Lower under control to keep your balance.
4. Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell over your midfoot.
2. Bend at the hips and knees and grip the bar just outside your legs.
3. Brace your core and keep your back flat.
4. Push through your heels and extend hips and knees to stand tall.
5. Lower the bar by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift.
2. Keep your back flat and chest up to protect your spine.
3. Brace your core hard before each pull.
4. Drive through your heels, not your toes.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
2. Pull your elbows back and drag the bar up along your torso.
3. Curl the bar to chest level, keeping it touching your body.
4. Lower the bar slowly back down along your torso.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows back so the bar stays against your body.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep your back straight and shoulders set.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
2. Pull your elbows back and drag the bar up along your torso.
3. Curl the bar to chest level, keeping it touching your body.
4. Lower the bar slowly back down along your torso.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows back so the bar stays against your body.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep your back straight and shoulders set.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.

instructions:
1. Set a bench behind you and hold a barbell across your front shoulders, elbows high.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, back to the bench.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower onto the bench.
4. Pause briefly without relaxing.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows high to hold the bar on your shoulders.
2. Brace your core to support your spine.
3. Stay upright and avoid leaning forward.
4. Control the descent and do not drop onto the bench.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell racked across the front of your shoulders. Keep elbows high and pointing forward.
2. Step forward with your right leg and lower until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
4. Push through your front heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows high so the bar stays on your shoulders.
2. Brace your core to protect your lower back and stay upright.
3. Lower with control and keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
4. Inhale as you step down, exhale as you drive up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell racked across the front of your shoulders. Keep elbows high and pointing forward.
2. Step forward with your right leg and lower until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Pause briefly at the bottom while keeping your torso upright.
4. Push through your front heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hold the pause without losing tension or letting the bar drift forward.
2. Keep elbows high so the bar stays on your shoulders.
3. Drive through the front heel to engage glutes and quads.
4. Keep your head up and eyes forward for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your thighs, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your arms nearly straight and your core braced.
3. Raise the barbell in front of you until it reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower it back to the start with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your shoulders, not by swinging your torso.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows to ease joint strain.
3. Brace your core to support your lower back.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell racked across the front of your shoulders. Keep elbows high and pointing forward.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your torso upright and chest tall throughout.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up, extending hips and knees fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows high to stop the bar rolling forward.
2. Brace your core hard to keep the torso upright.
3. Keep knees tracking over your toes.
4. Inhale at the top, exhale as you drive up.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Rest a barbell across your hips and hold it with both hands.
2. Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
3. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and hold briefly.
4. Lower your hips back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to load the glutes.
2. Keep knees in line with your toes, not flaring or caving.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a pad on the barbell for hip comfort.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell resting across your upper back.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and brace your core.
3. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at your hips to lower your torso forward.
4. Lower until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to raise your torso back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral spine the whole time to protect your lower back.
2. Push your hips back rather than rounding your back.
3. Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower down.
4. Start light to learn the hinge before adding load.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent and feet flat.
2. Roll a barbell over your hips and hold it in place with both hands.
3. Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top with hips fully extended.
5. Lower your hips back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to keep the load on your glutes.
2. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
3. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
4. Use a pad on the bar for comfort on your hips.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent and feet lifted, resting flat on the bench.
2. Grip the barbell slightly narrower than shoulder-width and hold it above your chest with arms extended.
3. Lower the bar to your lower chest while keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
4. Press the bar back up by extending your arms fully.
5. Repeat, then rack the bar safely.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked in to shift the work onto your triceps.
2. Keep your core braced since lifting your feet removes stability.
3. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
4. Use a spotter when lifting heavy.

instructions:
1. Lie on an incline bench set to about 30 to 45 degrees.
2. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and hold it above your upper chest with arms extended.
3. Lower the bar to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
4. Press the bar back up by extending your arms fully.
5. Repeat, then rack the bar safely.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep a firm grip for control and even bar path.
3. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
4. Use a spotter when lifting heavy.

instructions:
1. Stand over a barbell positioned between your legs in a split stance, one foot forward and one back.
2. Grip the bar with both hands, one in front and one behind your body, and stand it up.
3. Lower your hips by bending both knees until your back knee is just above the floor.
4. Push through your front heel to drive back up to standing.
5. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep the bar centered under your body throughout.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
3. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting from the offset load.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with hands shoulder-width apart and arms extended above your chest.
2. Lower the bar by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked toward your sides.
3. Bring the bar down and slightly back toward your upper chest and neck until your forearms near your biceps.
4. Drive the bar back up by extending your elbows, focusing on the triceps.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked, not flared, to load the triceps.
2. Lower the bar slowly and under control.
3. Use a weight light enough to keep the elbow path stable.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat with knees hip-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Sit back onto your heels, lowering your glutes toward your calves.
3. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
4. Drive your hips forward to return upright, squeezing your glutes at the top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
2. Keep your torso tall and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you sit back.
4. Pad your knees for comfort.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with palms up, shoulder-width apart, resting on your thighs near your knees.
2. Curl the bar up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms against your sides.
3. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
4. Lower the bar back toward your thighs under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still to isolate the biceps.
2. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Control the lowering phase fully.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Step out wide to the right, bending your right knee and pushing your hips back while keeping the left leg straight.
3. Keep your chest up and your right foot flat.
4. Push through your right heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push your hips back and sit into the bent leg.
2. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.
3. Track your knee over your foot, not past your toes.
4. Control the descent before driving back up.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or wedged into a corner, with the loaded end behind you.
2. Stand to the side, feet shoulder-width apart, then bend at the hips and knees with a flat back and grip the bar with one hand.
3. Start with your arm fully extended and the bar hanging down.
4. Pull the bar toward your side by driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade.
5. Lower the bar under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a flat, neutral spine throughout.
2. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working side.
3. Pull with your back, not just your arm.
4. Move the bar smoothly without jerking.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with a barbell resting across your upper back, hands gripping the bar just outside your shoulders.
2. Brace your core and step forward with one leg.
3. Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee nearly touches the ground.
4. Push through your front heel to return to the standing start position.
5. Alternate legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and your chest tall throughout the movement.
2. Drive through the front heel to engage the glutes and quads.
3. Take a long enough step so the front knee stays over the ankle.
4. Brace your core to keep the barbell stable.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with a barbell resting across your upper back, hands gripping the bar just outside your shoulders.
2. Step one leg forward into a split stance.
3. Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee nearly touches the ground.
4. Push through your front heel to rise back up, keeping your feet in place.
5. Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both feet planted in the same spot for each rep.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
3. Drive through the front heel to load the glutes and quads.
4. Push more through the back leg to return to the top.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a high flat bench with your chest supported and feet on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell below you with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended.
3. Pull the barbell toward your lower chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the barbell under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the back.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended above your chest.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the barbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Stop when you feel a stretch in the triceps.
5. Extend your elbows to press the barbell back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Lower the bar behind your head to stretch the long head.
3. Control the descent to protect your elbows.
4. Keep a firm grip throughout the set.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended above your chest.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the barbell toward your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Stop just above your forehead.
5. Extend your elbows to press the barbell back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms.
2. Lower the bar slowly under control to protect your forehead and elbows.
3. Keep your wrists straight and grip firm.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine or wedge it into a corner. Stand side-on to the bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the loaded end with the near hand. Let the arm hang straight.
3. Pull the bar toward your hip by driving the elbow up and back.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top.
5. Lower under control until the arm is fully extended. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the elbow back and up rather than just bending the arm.
2. Keep the hips square and brace the core to stop the torso twisting.
3. Keep a flat back throughout to protect the spine.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell across your upper back and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Stand with your feet closer than shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up and extend your hips and knees. Repeat.
tips:
1. The narrow stance shifts more load onto the quads, so control the descent.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
3. Brace your core before each rep to protect the lower back.
4. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you drive up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart with a loaded barbell beside one foot.
2. Hinge at the hips and slightly bend the knees to grip the bar with one hand, keeping the back flat.
3. Keep the bar close to your body and your shoulders square.
4. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand upright.
5. Lower the bar under control by hinging back at the hips. Switch arms. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your leg for a strong, efficient pull.
2. Brace your core hard to stop your torso twisting toward the loaded side.
3. Keep your shoulders level and back flat throughout.
4. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit with your upper back against a bench, knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Rest a padded barbell across your hips.
2. Lift one leg and extend it out in front of you.
3. Drive through the heel of the planted foot to raise your hips until your body forms a straight line.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and hold briefly.
5. Lower your hips under control, stopping just before they touch the floor. Switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel to bias the glutes.
2. Squeeze the glutes at the top rather than arching the lower back.
3. Keep your chin tucked and ribs down to stabilize the spine.
4. Use a pad on the bar for comfort on the hips.

instructions:
1. Hold a barbell overhead with arms locked out, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Brace your core and keep the bar stacked over your shoulders.
3. Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees are bent and the back knee hovers above the floor.
4. Drive through the front heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat with the other leg, alternating sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar directly over your shoulders, not drifting forward.
2. Brace your core to resist the torso tipping under the overhead load.
3. Keep the front shin near vertical and the chest tall.
4. Move slowly and stay balanced on each step.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a barbell overhead with both hands, grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms fully extended.
2. Brace your core and keep the bar stacked over your shoulders.
3. Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, keeping your arms locked out.
4. Pause and squeeze your traps at the top.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the barbell directly over your shoulders so your arms stay vertical.
2. Drive your shoulders straight up, not forward.
3. Brace your core to hold the bar steady overhead.
4. Use a weight light enough to keep the bar stable through the full range.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor over your mid-foot.
2. Bend at the hips and knees and grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor with a flat back.
3. Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest, driving your elbows up and back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to the floor with control and let it settle before the next rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso parallel to the floor for every rep.
2. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your lower back.
3. Drive your elbows up and back to lead with your back, not your arms.
4. Reset the bar on the floor between reps for a dead-stop pull.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor over your mid-foot.
2. Bend at the hips and knees and grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, back flat.
3. Drive through your legs to lift the bar, keeping it close to your body.
4. Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, then shrug and pull yourself under the bar.
5. Catch the bar in a front rack position with elbows forward and stand tall.
6. Lower the bar back to the floor with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power from an explosive hip extension, not your arms.
2. Keep the bar close to your body through the whole pull.
3. Drop fast under the bar to meet it in the rack position.
4. Practice with light weight to groove the technique before loading.

instructions:
1. Set the barbell on blocks just below knee height.
2. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, back flat.
3. Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar upward, keeping it close to your body.
4. Shrug and pull yourself under the bar.
5. Catch the bar in a front rack position with elbows forward and stand tall.
6. Lower the bar back to the blocks with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive explosively from the blocks to build force off a dead start.
2. Keep the bar close to your body as it rises.
3. Pull yourself under fast to catch the bar in the rack.
4. Reset the bar fully on the blocks between reps.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, barbell racked at shoulder height on your front deltoids, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Keep your chest up and core braced.
3. Dip straight down into a quarter squat, keeping your torso vertical.
4. Explosively drive up through your legs to launch the bar overhead.
5. Drop slightly and lock the bar out overhead with arms straight, then stand fully.
6. Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso vertical during the dip so the bar travels straight up.
2. Drive through your legs to power the bar overhead, not just your arms.
3. Keep the dip short and fast to transfer force into the bar.
4. Lock the bar out directly over the back of your head.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor over your mid-foot. Grip the bar with a wide overhand grip, hips down, back flat, arms straight.
2. Drive through your legs to lift the bar off the floor, keeping it close to your body.
3. As the bar passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug your shoulders.
4. Pull yourself under the bar and catch it overhead with arms locked out in a partial squat.
5. Stand up fully with the bar overhead, then lower it under control to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive power from your hips and legs, not your arms.
2. Keep the bar close to your body through the whole pull.
3. Catch the bar with locked arms and a braced core.
4. Keep your back flat during the lift off the floor.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Rest your upper arms on the pad and hold the barbell with an underhand grip, arms fully extended.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Lower the bar slowly to control the stretched position.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a weight you can move without leaning back.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell over your chest with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Bend your elbows and lower the bar in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
3. Pull the bar back over your chest.
4. Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then extend your arms to press it back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and ribs down to protect your lower back.
2. Control the bar through the full arc behind your head.
3. Inhale as you lower the bar, exhale as you press up.
4. Keep your upper arms steady during the triceps extension.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hinge at your hips and knees until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, back flat.
3. Pull the barbell toward your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. At the top, push the bar slightly down and pull it back up.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
4. Drive with your back, not your lower back swing.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell resting across your upper back. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering into a quarter squat with thighs above parallel.
3. Push through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees fully.
4. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
2. Brace your core hard, since quarter squats allow heavy loads.
3. Drive through your heels to engage the quads and glutes.
4. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell on a rack at just below knee height. Stand with feet hip-width apart, shins close to the bar.
2. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands just outside your knees.
3. Brace your core and pull your chest up to set a flat back.
4. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand tall.
5. Lock out with shoulders back and hips fully extended, keeping the bar against your legs.
6. Lower the bar back to the rack by hinging at the hips and bending the knees. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar in contact with your legs the whole lift.
2. Set a flat back before you pull and keep it neutral.
3. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top to finish the hip extension.
4. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your glutes with an overhand grip, hands just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Keep your back straight and core braced.
3. Lift the bar up and away from your body by raising your elbows out to the sides.
4. Squeeze your rear shoulders at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to the start with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
2. Keep the movement slow and avoid swinging the bar.
3. Use a light weight so the rear delts do the work.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on a sturdy box with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
2. Grip the bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width and brace your core.
3. Step one foot back off the box and lower into a lunge until the back knee nears the floor.
4. Keep the front knee over the ankle and torso upright.
5. Drive through the front heel to step back up onto the box.
6. Alternate legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
2. Lower under control to use the added range from the box.
3. Drive through the front heel to load the glutes.
4. Keep your torso tall and core tight for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
2. Grip the bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width and brace your core.
3. Step one foot back and lower into a lunge until the back knee nears the floor.
4. Keep the front knee over the ankle and torso upright.
5. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Alternate legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
2. Lower under control through the full range.
3. Drive through the front heel to engage the glutes.
4. Keep your core braced to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width.
2. Let the bar hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.
3. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your forearms at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to the start with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists firm and straight throughout.
2. Avoid swinging or using your shoulders to lift.
3. Use a lighter weight than a standard curl, the grip is harder.
4. Lower slowly to load the forearms.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip the barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with arms extended.
4. Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
5. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides through the whole movement.
2. Use a spotter, as the underhand grip is harder to control.
3. Lower the bar slowly and under control.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip the barbell with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with arms extended.
4. Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked.
5. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked to drive the bar along a low-to-high path.
2. Use a spotter, as the underhand grip is harder to control.
3. Lower the bar slowly and under control.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Bend at the hips and knees until your torso is near parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
3. Pull the barbell toward your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the barbell with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and core braced to protect your spine.
2. Pull with your back, not just your arms.
3. Exhale as you row up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the bar close to your body throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest and stomach supported.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms hanging straight down.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze at the top with your knuckles facing up.
5. Lower the barbell with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your chest firmly into the bench to keep your upper arms still.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the muscle.
4. Keep your wrists firm and straight.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat with a loaded barbell on the floor in front of you.
2. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Brace your core and roll the bar forward, extending your arms and body.
4. Roll out as far as you can while keeping your back flat and hips from sagging.
5. Pull the bar back to the start using your abdominals.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stop your lower back from arching.
2. Do not let your hips sag or pike.
3. Only roll out as far as you can control.
4. Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, hands just outside your hips.
2. Keep your back flat, chest up, and knees slightly bent.
3. Push your hips back and slide the barbell down the front of your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
4. Lower the bar to just below your knees while keeping your spine neutral.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the barbell touching your legs the whole time.
2. Hinge at the hips, do not round your lower back.
3. Push your hips back instead of squatting down.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower the bar.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor and your back upright.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width, resting behind your neck at shoulder height.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell with control back to behind your neck.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
2. Only use this exercise if you have good shoulder mobility.
3. Lower the bar under control to protect the shoulder joint.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs spread and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Lean forward and rest the backs of your upper arms against your inner thighs.
4. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Lower the barbell with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed against your thighs to isolate the biceps.
2. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top of each rep.
3. Control the lowering phase, do not let the bar drop.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit upright on a bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Rest a barbell across your upper back, holding it with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
3. Keep your back flat and hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso toward your thighs.
4. Stop when your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
5. Lift your torso back up to the upright position by extending your hips and lower back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral, do not round your back.
2. Move slowly and under control in both directions.
3. Brace your core before each rep.
4. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor and your back upright against the support.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, at shoulder height in front of you.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell with control back to shoulder height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and torso upright throughout.
2. Press the bar in a straight line over your head.
3. Lower the bar under control to shoulder level.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Rest a barbell across your thighs, just above your knees, and hold it steady.
3. Press through the balls of your feet and lift your heels as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hold the barbell firmly against your thighs so it does not shift.
2. Pause and squeeze hard at the top for full calf contraction.
3. Lower slowly through a full range of motion.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
name: Barbell seated on knee calve raises

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Rest the bar at shoulder height in front of you.
4. Press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the bar back to shoulder height with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and back against the bench for stability.
2. Drive the bar straight up, not forward.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.
name: Barbell seated overhead press

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and back upright.
2. Hold a barbell with a close overhand grip, hands narrower than shoulder-width.
3. Raise the bar overhead, then lower it behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing up.
4. Extend your elbows to press the bar back overhead until your arms are straight.
5. Lower the bar behind your head again with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing up and close to your head.
2. Move only at the elbows; keep your upper arms still.
3. Control the bar through a full stretch behind your head.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
name: Barbell seated overhead triceps press

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Rest a barbell across your upper back, holding it with a wide overhand grip.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced.
4. Rotate your torso to the right while keeping your hips and legs still.
5. Rotate back through center and twist to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to protect your spine.
2. Keep your hips and legs locked in place; only the torso turns.
3. Move smoothly and avoid jerking the bar.
4. Use a light load to keep control through the full range.
name: Barbell seated twist

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Rest a barbell across your upper back, holding it with a wide overhand grip.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced to stay balanced.
4. Rotate your torso to the right while keeping your hips and legs still.
5. Rotate back through center and twist to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Plant your feet wide for a stable base on the ball.
2. Brace your core to control balance and protect your spine.
3. Keep your hips still; rotate only through the torso.
4. Use a light load and move smoothly.
name: Barbell seated twist on exercise ball

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
2. Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.
3. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your traps at the top.
5. Lower your shoulders with control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and let the traps do the work.
2. Do not roll the shoulders; lift straight up and down.
3. Hold the squeeze briefly at the top for full contraction.
4. Use a controlled tempo to keep tension on the traps.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
2. Keep your back straight and core braced.
3. Bend at the waist to the right, lowering your torso as far as is comfortable.
4. Engage your obliques to return to upright.
5. Bend to the left side in the same way.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Bend only sideways; do not twist the torso.
2. Exhale as you bend, inhale as you return.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
4. Keep your hips facing forward and stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, holding a barbell across your upper back.
2. Keep your back straight and core braced.
3. Shift your weight onto your right leg and bend the right knee, keeping the left leg straight.
4. Lower until the right thigh is parallel to the floor, knee tracking over the foot.
5. Push through the right heel to return to center, then repeat on the left side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and chest up throughout.
2. Keep the heel of the bending leg flat on the floor.
3. Drive through the heel to engage the glutes.
4. Feel the stretch in the straight-leg adductors.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell in one hand with an underhand grip.
2. Let the arm hang at full length by your side.
3. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulder by bending the elbow.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell with control to full extension, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm still to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not swing the body or use momentum.
3. Lower slowly to load the muscle on the way down.
4. Keep the wrist firm and neutral.

instructions:
1. Stand on your right leg, holding a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip.
2. Keep your back straight and core braced.
3. Hinge at the hip, lifting the left leg straight behind you as the barbell lowers.
4. Lower until your torso and left leg are near parallel to the floor, right knee slightly bent.
5. Drive the hip forward to return to standing, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat; do not round the spine.
2. Move slowly to stay balanced on the standing leg.
3. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your hips level and square to the floor.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a barbell across your upper back, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Place one foot back on a bench, front foot planted about 60 cm ahead.
3. Bend your front knee and lower until your front thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your front heel to stand back up.
5. Finish all reps on one leg, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and torso tall.
2. Track your front knee over your foot.
3. Lower under control, do not bounce at the bottom.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width, barbell over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
2. Grip the bar wide with palms facing down and set a flat back.
3. Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar up, keeping it close.
4. Pull yourself under and catch the bar overhead with straight arms in a squat.
5. Stand up tall with the bar locked out overhead.
6. Lower the bar and repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the floor and finish with full hip extension.
2. Keep the bar close to your body the whole pull.
3. Drop fast under the bar to catch it stable overhead.
4. Use a weight you can control with clean technique.

instructions:
1. Stand with the barbell across your upper back, hands in a wide snatch grip.
2. Set your feet about shoulder-width with a tall torso.
3. Dip slightly by bending your knees and hips.
4. Drive up fast, then push yourself under the bar into a deep squat.
5. Catch the bar overhead with straight arms and stand up tall.
6. Lower the bar and repeat.
tips:
1. Drive hard with your legs to move the bar up.
2. Drop quickly and aggressively under the bar.
3. Lock your arms and keep the bar over your mid-foot.
4. Brace your core to stay stable in the catch.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width, barbell over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
2. Grip the bar with palms down, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, and set a flat back.
3. Lift the bar by extending your hips and knees together, keeping it close to your body.
4. Stand fully upright with the bar at hip level.
5. Lower the bar under control by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up the whole lift.
2. Keep the bar close to your legs.
3. Push through your mid-foot as you stand.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width, barbell over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
2. Grip the bar with palms down, hands set wide in a snatch grip, and flatten your back.
3. Lift the bar by extending your hips and knees together, keeping it close to your body.
4. Stand fully upright with the bar at hip level.
5. Lower the bar under control by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and shoulders pulled back.
2. The wide grip lowers your hips, so push hard with your legs off the floor.
3. Keep the bar close to your body.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Set the barbell on blocks at knee height. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
2. Grip the bar wide with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width. Set a flat back and brace.
3. Pull the bar off the blocks, keeping it close to your body.
4. As the bar passes the hips, explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles and pull the bar upward.
5. Drop under the bar into a squat and catch it overhead with arms locked out.
6. Stand up with the bar overhead, then lower it back to the blocks. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive hard through the legs and hips to launch the bar.
2. Pull yourself under the bar fast to catch it in a stable overhead position.
3. Keep the bar close to your body during the pull.
4. Keep arms locked overhead and shoulders active in the catch.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, the bar over your mid-foot close to your shins.
2. Grip the bar wide with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width. Set a flat back and brace.
3. Lift the bar by extending hips and knees together, keeping it close to your body.
4. As the bar passes the hips, explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles and pull the bar up to about abdomen height, driving the elbows up and out.
5. Lower the bar under control by bending the hips and knees. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body for an efficient pull.
2. Finish the pull with a full, aggressive hip extension.
3. Lead the upward pull with the elbows, not the hands.
4. Keep a flat back and braced core throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, the bar over your mid-foot close to your shins.
2. Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Set a flat back and brace.
3. Lift the bar by extending hips and knees together, keeping it close to your body.
4. As the bar passes the hips, explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles and pull the bar upward.
