5. Drop into a split stance, one foot forward and one back, and catch the bar on the shoulders with elbows pointing forward.
6. Bring the feet back together, then lower the bar under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.
2. Drive hard through the legs and hips to launch the bar.
3. Drop fast into the split stance to catch the bar securely.
4. Keep the chest up and elbows high in the catch.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar at shoulder height with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Keep the chest up, elbows slightly forward, and brace your core.
3. Dip by bending the knees and hips a short distance.
4. Explosively extend the knees and hips to drive the bar overhead.
5. Split the feet into a lunge, one forward and one back, and catch the bar overhead with arms locked.
6. Bring the feet back together, then lower the bar to the shoulders under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the bar up with the legs, not the arms.
2. Keep the dip short and straight down.
3. Split fast and lock the arms to catch in a stable position.
4. Keep the torso upright and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Place a barbell across your upper back and stand in a split stance, one foot forward and one back.
2. Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
3. Lower by bending both knees until the back knee nearly touches the floor and the front thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Keep the front knee tracking over the front foot.
5. Push through the front heel to stand back up, extending both knees.
6. Finish the set, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee in line with the front foot.
2. Move slowly and under control through both phases.
3. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the torso tall to load the quads, or lean slightly forward to load the glutes.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up and extend your hips and knees fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Track your knees in line with your toes.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid rounding your lower back.
3. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand up.
4. Keep the bar over your midfoot throughout.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower as deep as possible, hips below the knees.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up and extend your hips and knees fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Only go as deep as you can keep a neutral spine without your pelvis tucking under.
2. Track your knees over your toes.
3. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you drive up.
4. Keep your heels flat and weight over your midfoot.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower until your hips drop below your knees.
4. Hold the bottom position.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up and extend your hips and knees fully.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay tight in the hold and do not relax at the bottom.
2. Track your knees in line with your toes.
3. Keep your chest up and your lower back neutral during the pause.
4. Inhale before descending and exhale as you stand up.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a barbell behind your glutes with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
2. Let your arms hang straight with the bar resting against the back of your thighs.
3. Curl the bar up by flexing your wrists only.
4. Squeeze your forearms at the top for a moment.
5. Lower the bar slowly by extending your wrists.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms and shoulders still and move only at the wrists.
2. Use a controlled tempo through the full range.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced as the bar hangs behind you.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip slightly closer than shoulder-width.
2. Let your arms hang straight with the bar against your thighs.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the bar slowly.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not swing or use momentum to lift the bar.
3. Control the lowering phase fully.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep the bar path close to your face and head.
5. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stop your lower back arching.
2. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
3. The close grip loads the triceps harder, so keep elbows tracking forward.
4. Squeeze your glutes to keep your torso stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip at thigh level.
2. Hinge forward at your hips so your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
3. Let your arms hang straight down with elbows fixed.
4. Curl the barbell up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Lower the barbell under control until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows still so the biceps do all the work.
2. Do not swing your torso or use momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top of each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand on a raised step with your forefeet on the edge and heels hanging off.
2. Rest a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip.
3. Set your feet shoulder-width apart and stand tall.
4. Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.
5. Lower your heels below the level of the step to stretch the calves.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid bouncing at the bottom.
2. Drive up through the balls of your feet.
3. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
4. Get a full stretch by dropping the heels below the step.

instructions:
1. Stand on a raised step with your forefeet on the edge and heels hanging off.
2. Rest a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Set your feet shoulder-width apart and stand tall.
4. Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.
5. Lower your heels below the level of the step to stretch the calves.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid bouncing at the bottom.
2. Drive up through the balls of your feet.
3. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
4. Get a full stretch by dropping the heels below the step.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep the bar path close to your face and head.
5. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stop your lower back arching.
2. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
3. Drive your head slightly forward once the bar clears it.
4. Squeeze your glutes to keep your torso stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell overhead with a close overhand grip and arms fully extended.
2. Keep your upper arms close to your head and stationary.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the barbell behind your head until your forearms are about parallel to the floor.
4. Press the barbell back up by extending your arms fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and close to your head to isolate the triceps.
2. Move slowly and under control, especially while lowering.
3. Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Drive the bar in a straight line close to your face.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep wrists stacked over your forearms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips facing forward.
3. Rotate your torso to the right under control.
4. Return to center, then rotate your torso to the left.
5. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Rotate from your torso, not just your arms.
2. Keep your hips and knees facing forward to isolate the obliques.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return to center.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let your arms hang fully extended with the bar against your thighs.
3. Curl the barbell up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to isolate the biceps.
2. Avoid swinging your body or using momentum.
3. Lower the bar slowly to keep tension on the muscle.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip set just wider than shoulders.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.
2. Keep the bar path straight and close to your face.
3. Do not flare your elbows too far out at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a stable bench with a barbell across your upper back, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Place your right foot flat on the bench.
3. Push through your right heel to lift your body up and stand tall on the bench.
4. Step down with your left foot, then your right foot, back to the floor.
5. Switch the leading leg and repeat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push through the heel of the leading foot to drive the lift.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid pushing off the trailing foot.
3. Exhale as you step up, inhale as you step down.
4. Make sure the bench is stable before loading the bar.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip against your thighs.
2. Keep your knees almost straight with only a slight bend.
3. Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back to lower the bar down the front of your legs.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand and lift the bar back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Hinge at the hips, not the lower back.
3. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip against your thighs.
2. Keep your legs straight but not locked.
3. Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back to lower the bar down the front of your legs.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand and lift the bar back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Hinge at the hips, not the lower back.
3. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out, bar over your midfoot.
2. Hinge down and grip the bar with both hands inside your legs, using an overhand grip.
3. Set your back flat, chest up, and hips down.
4. Drive through your heels, extending your hips and knees together to lift the bar.
5. Stand tall, then lower the bar to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.
2. Drive your knees out over your toes as you lift.
3. Push the floor away through your heels.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out, holding a barbell with an overhand grip against your thighs.
2. Keep your knees softly bent and your back flat.
3. Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back to lower the bar down your legs.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings and inner thighs.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand and lift the bar back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and hinge from the hips.
2. Push your knees out in line with your toes.
3. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip and hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let your arms hang straight with the bar resting against your thighs.
3. Keep your upper arms still and curl the bar up to shoulder level by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides.
2. Do not swing your torso or use momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. The wide grip shifts emphasis to the inner short head of the biceps.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip and hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let the bar rest against your thighs with your arms straight.
3. Pull the bar straight up the front of your body by lifting your elbows out to the sides.
4. Stop when the bar reaches chest height, keeping your elbows above your wrists.
5. Lower the bar under control to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead the movement with your elbows, not your hands.
2. Keep your chest up and torso upright.
3. The wide grip targets the side and rear delts more than a narrow grip.
4. Stop at chest height to protect your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip and hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let the bar rest against your thighs with your arms straight.
3. Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
4. Hold the top position for a moment.
5. Lower your shoulders under control to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and let your traps do the work.
2. Move your shoulders straight up, not in a rolling circle.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a controlled pace rather than jerking the weight.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
2. Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging just past your knees.
3. Lower the bar by letting your wrists extend fully under control.
4. Curl the bar up by flexing your wrists as high as possible.
5. Keep your forearms pressed to your thighs throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearms still so only your wrists move.
2. Use a full range of motion at the wrist.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Let the bar roll to your fingertips at the bottom for a fuller stretch.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs spread wide and feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
2. Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging over your knees.
3. Lower the bar by letting your wrists extend fully under control.
4. Curl the bar up by flexing your wrists as high as possible.
5. Keep your forearms pressed to your thighs throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearms still so only your wrists move.
2. Use a full range of motion at the wrist.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. The wide-leg position gives your wrists more room to travel.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Rest your forearms on your thighs so your wrists hang over your knees.
3. Lower the bar by letting your wrists drop as far as they go.
4. Lift the bar by extending your wrists upward as high as possible.
5. Keep your forearms pressed to your thighs the whole time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearms still and move only at the wrists.
2. Use a controlled tempo on the way down.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a light load to keep the wrists pain-free.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your legs as straight as possible.
3. Bend at the hips and reach your hands toward your toes.
4. Hold the stretch for a few seconds.
5. Stand back up under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge from the hips, not the lower back.
2. Move slowly with no bouncing.
3. Breathe deeply to relax into the stretch.
4. Bend the knees slightly if your hamstrings are tight.

instructions:
1. Start in a quarter squat with feet shoulder-width apart and hands as if holding a ball.
2. Drive up explosively, extending your hips, knees, and ankles to jump.
3. Reach your arms overhead as if shooting.
4. Land softly on the balls of your feet, then your whole foot.
5. Bend your knees to absorb the landing and return to the squat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive power from your legs and hips, not your arms.
2. Land soft with bent knees to protect your joints.
3. Keep your chest up through the jump.
4. Exhale as you jump.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with the thigh pad set against your legs.
2. Grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip.
3. Keep your torso upright and tilt your head slightly forward.
4. Pull the bar down behind your neck while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Slowly return the bar to the top with arms fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull with your back, not your arms.
2. Avoid pulling the bar too low to protect the neck and shoulders.
3. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
4. Keep the movement slow and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and the band under your feet.
2. Hold the band ends at your shoulders with elbows bent and the band behind your neck.
3. Brace your core.
4. Press the band straight overhead until your arms are extended.
5. Lower the band back behind your neck under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stay stable.
2. Press in a straight line overhead.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Only press as low as your shoulder mobility allows.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a stable bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Step up onto the bench with your right foot.
3. Drive through the right heel and bring your left foot up to stand fully on the bench.
4. Step down with the left foot, then the right foot.
5. Repeat, alternating the leading foot each time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Make sure the bench is stable before you start.
2. Keep your chest up and torso upright throughout.
3. Drive through the heel of the stepping leg, not the toes.
4. Lower yourself with control instead of dropping down.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench with your back to it.
2. Place the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
3. Keep your torso upright and your right foot flat.
4. Bend your right knee to lower your body until your right thigh is near parallel.
5. Push through your right heel to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot, not caving inward.
3. Place the front foot far enough forward to protect the knee.
4. Lower and rise with an even, controlled tempo.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench with your back to it.
2. Place the top of your right foot on the bench behind you.
3. Keep your torso upright and your left foot flat.
4. Bend your left knee to lower your body until your left thigh is near parallel.
5. Push through your left heel to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot, not caving inward.
3. Place the front foot far enough forward to protect the knee.
4. Lower and rise with an even, controlled tempo.

instructions:
1. Lie back on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Cross your hands over your chest or place them behind your head.
3. Tuck your chin slightly to keep a neutral neck.
4. Engage your core and lift your upper body toward your knees.
5. Lower back down with control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chin slightly tucked to protect your neck.
2. Squeeze your abs hard at the top of the movement.
3. Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
4. Avoid pulling on your head with your hands.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench with hands beside your hips, fingers forward.
2. Slide your hips off the bench, supporting your weight on your hands.
3. Bend your knees to about 90 degrees with feet flat on the floor.
4. Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your palms to press back up to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing backward and close to your body.
2. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
3. Keep your chest up and back close to the bench.
4. Lower with control to protect the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips.
2. Walk your feet out, extend your legs, and shift your weight onto your heels as you lift your hips off the bench, arms straight.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor.
4. Stop when your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
5. Press through your hands to raise your hips back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing back and close to your body.
2. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
3. Lower under control, do not drop into the bottom.
4. Breathe out as you press up.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands beside your hips for support.
2. Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor with your legs extended.
3. Pull your knees toward your chest while bracing your core.
4. Extend your legs back out under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced through the whole movement.
2. Do not swing your legs, use your abs to pull the knees in.
3. Breathe out as you tuck the knees in.
4. Keep the movement slow and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand under a pull-up bar with one foot resting on a bench for support.
2. Grip the bar with both hands, overhand, shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
4. Use your foot on the bench only as much as needed for assistance.
5. Lower yourself back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Make sure the bench is stable and your foot is firmly placed.
2. Pull from your back, not just your arms.
3. Pack your shoulders down before each rep to engage the lats.
4. Breathe out as you pull up.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a bench with your legs extended and your hands on the floor under your shoulders, arms straight.
2. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
3. Squeeze your glutes and brace your core to hold the line.
4. Hold the position with steady breathing.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard to keep the hips lifted.
2. Keep a straight line from head to heels, do not let the hips sag.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Breathe steadily, do not hold your breath.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips.
2. Walk your feet out, extend your legs, and lift your hips off the bench, arms straight.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your hips while bending your knees to pull your heels in.
4. Stop when your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
5. Press through your hands and extend your legs to raise your hips back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing back and close to your body.
2. Move the dip and the leg curl together in one smooth motion.
3. Keep your core braced for stability.
4. Breathe out as you press up.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and grip the front edge near your hips.
2. Walk your feet forward and straighten your legs, keeping heels on the floor.
3. Lift your hips off the bench and support your weight on your hands.
4. Bend your elbows straight back and lower your hips until your arms reach 90 degrees.
5. Press through your hands to straighten your arms and lift back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing back, not flaring out, to load the triceps.
2. Stay close to the bench to protect your shoulders.
3. Lower under control and avoid dropping into the bottom.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Stand next to a wall.
2. Raise one arm to shoulder height and bend the elbow to 90 degrees.
3. Place your forearm and palm flat against the wall.
4. Turn your torso slowly away from the wall until you feel a stretch across your chest.
5. Hold, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder down and away from your ear.
2. Rotate the torso slowly to control the stretch depth.
3. Stop at a mild stretch, not pain.
4. Breathe deeply and steadily.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Keeping the right knee bent at 90 degrees, lift the leg back and up until the thigh is in line with your torso.
3. Lower the knee back to the start.
4. Lift the right knee out to the side until the thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the knee back to the start, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute at the top of each kick.
2. Keep your back flat and head neutral, looking at the floor.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms out to the sides in a T shape.
2. Bend your knees and lift your feet so the thighs are vertical.
3. Keeping shoulders flat, lower both knees to one side.
4. Bring the knees back to the center.
5. Lower both knees to the opposite side, then return to center.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both shoulders flat on the floor throughout.
2. Move slowly and with control to protect your back.
3. Lower the knees only as far as your shoulders stay down.
4. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with arms out to the sides in a T shape.
2. Rest your bent legs on top of a stability ball.
3. Keeping shoulders flat, roll your knees and the ball to one side.
4. Bring the knees and ball back to the center.
5. Roll to the opposite side, then return to center.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both shoulders flat on the floor throughout.
2. Control the ball so it does not roll away from you.
3. Move slowly to engage the obliques and protect your back.
4. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, wrists under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Keep your right leg bent at 90 degrees.
3. Raise your right knee out to the side until your thigh is level with your hip.
4. Lower your knee back to the floor under control.
5. Finish the set, then switch to the left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists under your shoulders for a stable base.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level, do not rotate your torso.
3. Lift with the outer hip and glute, not by leaning to the opposite side.
4. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip just outside your knees.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let the bar hang with your arms straight.
4. Pull the bar to your lower chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and your core braced throughout.
2. Drive your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
3. Do not use momentum or jerk the bar with your lower back.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and your core braced to protect your lower back.
2. Lead with your elbows and lift with your rear shoulders, not your traps or arms.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows the whole time.
4. Use a controlled motion and avoid swinging the weights up.

instructions:
1. Stand on the resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one end in each hand.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let your arms hang down with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Raise your arms out to the sides into a T shape, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower your arms under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and your core braced to protect your lower back.
2. Lead with your elbows and lift with your rear shoulders.
3. Adjust your stance on the band to set the tension.
4. Control the return, do not let the band snap your arms down.

instructions:
1. Stand on the resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one handle in each hand.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let your arms hang down with the band under tension.
4. Pull the handles toward your hips by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower your arms under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows close to your body to load the back muscles.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Keep your back flat and core braced throughout.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
3. Let the bar hang at arm's length below your shoulders, back flat.
4. Pull the bar toward your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and core braced to protect your spine.
2. Drive with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
3. Do not use momentum or jerk the bar with your hips.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar across your shoulders behind your neck.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your knees slightly bent and core braced.
4. Rotate your torso to one side, driving one end of the bar upward.
5. Return to center, then rotate to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your lower back.
2. Rotate from the trunk, not just the arms.
3. Move under control to feel the obliques work.
4. Breathe steadily to keep the core braced.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and arms extended.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back.
2. Hold your upper arms still so the biceps do the work.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
4. Lower slowly to keep tension on the muscle.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and arms extended.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back.
2. Hold your upper arms still so the biceps do the work.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
4. Lower slowly to keep constant tension.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an underhand grip wider than shoulder width.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and arms extended.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back.
2. The wide grip emphasizes the inner biceps, so keep elbows fixed.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
4. Lower slowly to keep constant tension.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a cable crossover machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grab a low pulley handle in each hand with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width, arms extended down.
3. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides and curl both handles up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the handles under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back to lift the load.
2. Keep your upper arms still so the biceps do the work.
3. Lower the handles slowly to keep tension on the muscle.
4. The cable keeps tension at the top, so pause and squeeze each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended forward, palms up.
2. Step forward with your right foot and tap the floor lightly.
3. At the same time, curl both hands toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Return your right foot and extend your arms back to the start.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your knees for balance.
2. Keep your upper arms still so the biceps do the work.
3. Move slowly and under control.
4. Brace your core to stay stable through each step.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of the band.
2. Hold a handle in each hand, palms forward, arms extended down at your sides.
3. Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the handles toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the handles under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and core braced.
2. Do not swing your body to lift the band.
3. The band gets harder near the top, so control the squeeze.
4. Lower slowly to keep tension on the biceps.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of the band.
2. Hold a handle in each hand, palms forward, arms extended down at your sides.
3. Curl the handles toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Rotate your palms to face forward and press the handles overhead until your arms are extended.
5. Reverse the motion to lower the handles back to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep your torso upright.
2. Move slowly and under control through both phases.
3. Exhale as you press overhead and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your wrists straight under the handles.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs apart and feet flat on the floor.
2. Rest the elbow of your working arm against the inside of your thigh.
3. Grab under your thigh or hamstring with that hand.
4. Curl your hand up toward your shoulder by bending your elbow, resisting with your leg.
5. Lower under control until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm braced against your thigh to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not use momentum to move the arm.
3. Use your leg to provide steady resistance both up and down.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Clasp your hands together behind your back.
3. Straighten your arms and lift them slightly away from your body.
4. Pull your shoulders back until you feel a stretch in the front of your upper arms.
5. Hold, then release.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest open and shoulders pulled back.
2. Do not arch your lower back to reach further.
3. Adjust your grip width so you feel the stretch in the upper arm, not the wrists.
4. Breathe out slowly to help the muscle relax.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and lift your hips off the floor.
2. Support your hips with your hands, keeping your elbows on the floor.
3. Extend your right leg straight forward while bending your left knee toward your torso.
4. Switch legs, extending the left leg and bending the right knee.
5. Keep a steady, controlled pedaling motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Support your lower back firmly with your hands.
2. Engage your core to control the leg motion.
3. Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
4. Slow down if your lower back starts to arch.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your hands behind your head.
2. Raise your legs to about 45 degrees off the floor, keeping them straight.
3. Bring your right knee toward your chest while twisting to touch your left elbow to it.
4. Switch sides, bringing your left knee in and your right elbow toward it.
5. Continue alternating in a controlled, bicycle-like motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist using your core, not your neck or shoulders.
2. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
3. Do not pull on your neck with your hands.
4. Exhale as you rotate.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your legs bent and lifted off the floor.
2. Keep both arms flat on the floor beside you.
3. Bring your right knee toward your chest while straightening your left leg without touching the floor.
4. Switch sides, bringing the left knee in and straightening the right leg.
5. Continue alternating in a controlled, bicycle-like motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use your abs to control the leg movement.
2. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
3. Keep the motion slow and controlled.
4. Do not let the extended leg touch the floor.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your hands behind your head and legs lifted off the floor.
2. Bring your right knee toward your chest while extending your left leg out.
3. Twist your torso to touch your left elbow to your right knee.
4. Switch sides, bringing the left knee in and your right elbow toward it.
5. Continue alternating in a controlled, bicycle-like motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist using your core, not your neck or shoulders.
2. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
3. Keep your elbows wide and do not pull on your head.
4. Exhale as you rotate.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Brace your core and keep your spine neutral.
3. Extend your right arm forward and your left leg back until both are parallel to the floor.
4. Hold briefly, keeping your hips and shoulders square.
5. Return to the start and switch to the left arm and right leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stop your lower back from sagging.
2. Move slowly and keep your hips level, do not rotate.
3. Look down at the floor to keep your neck neutral.
4. Exhale as you extend the limbs.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Brace your core and keep your spine neutral.
3. Extend your right arm forward and your left leg back, raising both slightly above torso level.
4. Hold briefly, keeping your hips and shoulders square.
5. Return to the start and switch to the left arm and right leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stop your lower back from sagging.
2. Do not lift the leg so high that your lower back arches.
3. Move slowly and keep your hips level, do not rotate.
4. Look down at the floor to keep your neck neutral.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you.
2. Lean back slightly and lift your legs off the floor, balancing on your sit bones.
3. Straighten your legs so your body forms a V shape.
4. Reach your arms forward at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
5. Keep your chest lifted and your back straight, and hold.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift your chest and keep your back straight, do not let it round.
2. Brace your core to stay balanced.
3. Bend the knees slightly if you cannot keep the back straight.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
3. Push through your forearms to rock your body back, moving your shoulders behind your elbows.
4. Pull with your forearms to rock your body forward, moving your shoulders ahead of your elbows.
5. Keep the motion slow and controlled.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line, do not let your hips drop.
2. Move slowly to keep the core under constant tension.
3. Exhale as you rock forward, inhale as you rock back.
4. Use sliders or a towel under your feet for a smooth glide.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and your knees slightly bent.
2. Raise your arms straight out at shoulder height.
3. Keep your upper body still and shift your hips to the left.
4. Shift your hips back to the right under control.
5. Continue moving your hips side to side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep your upper body from swaying.
2. Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
3. Keep your knees slightly bent for a fuller range of motion.
4. Keep your feet flat and pointing forward.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down until hips reach knee level, arms reaching back at your sides.
2. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
3. Drive through your feet and stand up explosively, rising onto your toes.
4. Swing both arms overhead as you extend.
5. Lower back into the squat with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the power from your legs and hips, not your arms.
2. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your chest up and back flat in the squat.
4. Control the descent to protect your knees.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso.
3. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
4. Press through your palms to push your body back up to the plank.
5. Keep your core tight throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows close to the body to load the triceps.
2. Brace your core to hold a straight line.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.
4. Do not let your hips sag.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
4. Raise your arms out to the sides until level with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower your arms with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a flat back and braced core throughout.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Keep a slight bend in the elbows.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands on hips or at your sides for balance.
2. Keep your legs straight.
3. Lift your heels off the floor and rise onto your toes.
4. Hold briefly at the top and squeeze your calves.
5. Lower your heels with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rise as high as possible for full range.
2. Move slowly and pause at the top.
3. Keep weight balanced over your toes.
4. Stand tall with chest up for stability.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands on hips or at your sides.
2. Step forward with one foot.
3. Lower your body until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee near the floor.
4. Keep your front knee over your ankle and torso upright.
5. Push through your front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over your toes.
3. Lower with control and avoid bouncing.
4. Take a long enough step to load the glutes.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and reach both arms straight overhead.
2. Swing your arms down hard in front of your body as if slamming a ball to the floor.
3. Bend your knees into a quarter squat as your hands drop past your hips.
4. Drive back up and lift your arms overhead to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core and crunch as you slam the arms down.
2. Keep your back flat, do not round the spine.
3. Move explosively but control the return.
4. Exhale on the downward slam.

instructions:
1. Stand in a squat with feet shoulder-width apart and arms hanging between your thighs.
2. Straighten your legs to stand up tall.
3. Raise both arms straight overhead as you rise.
4. Lower back into the squat and bring your arms down between your thighs.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral spine throughout the movement.
2. Track your knees over your toes during the squat.
3. Control the descent back into the squat.
4. Exhale as you stand and raise the arms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms close to your knees.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Raise both arms straight overhead as you squat.
4. Stand back up and bring your arms back to your knees.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral spine and do not round your back.
2. Track your knees over your toes during the squat.
3. Move the arms at a controlled pace.
4. Exhale as you stand back up.

instructions:
1. Stand in a squat with feet shoulder-width apart and hands in front of your knees.
2. Straighten your legs to stand up tall.
3. Press both hands straight overhead as you rise.
4. Lower back into the squat and bring your hands in front of your knees.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral spine throughout the movement.
2. Track your knees over your toes during the squat.
3. Use leg drive to power the press overhead.
4. Exhale as you stand and press.

instructions:
1. Stand in a partial lunge with your left foot forward and right foot back, hands in front of your hips.
2. Drive your right knee forward and up to hip level.
3. Bring your hands down to meet your knee.
4. Lower your right leg back to the partial lunge.
5. Switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your supporting leg slightly bent for stability.
2. Drive the knee up powerfully while staying balanced.
3. Brace your core to control the torso.
4. Breathe steadily through the movement.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight and together.
2. Rest your forehead on your hands and press your hips into the floor.
3. Bend your knees to pull your heels toward your glutes.
4. Squeeze your hamstrings at the top.
5. Lower your feet back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and thighs pressed into the floor throughout.
2. Do not arch your lower back to lift your feet higher.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the hamstrings.
4. Flex your feet to keep the calves engaged.

instructions:
1. Hang from the bar with arms fully extended and body straight.
2. Pull explosively, driving your chest up toward the bar.
3. Lean forward and transition your shoulders over the bar.
4. Press down to push your body up until your arms are straight.
5. Lower back through the transition to the hanging position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to control swing during the transition.
2. Use an explosive pull to clear the bar.
3. Lean your torso forward early to make the transition easier.
4. Control the descent to protect your shoulders and elbows.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended straight overhead.
2. Keep your chest up and arms locked overhead.
3. Bend your knees and hips to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Keep the arms overhead and your torso upright.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stabilize the overhead position.
2. Keep your arms locked and aligned over your midfoot.
3. Track your knees in line with your toes.
4. Keep your chest lifted to avoid leaning forward.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Clasp your hands together and extend your arms overhead, elbows slightly bent.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your hands behind your head.
4. Keep your upper arms still and close to your head.
5. Extend your arms back to the overhead position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and close to your ears.
2. Brace your core to avoid arching your back.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the triceps.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch, then drive back up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
2. Step forward with one foot into a lunge, front knee over the ankle.
3. Lower until the back knee is close to the floor.
4. Pulse up and down with small movements in the lunge.
5. Push through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced for balance.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.
3. Pulse with control and steady tempo.
4. Press through the front heel to drive the working leg.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips or extended in front of you.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
3. Raise up a few cm, then lower back to the parallel position in a small pulse.
4. Keep pulsing in the lower range with control.
5. Stand back up to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and weight over your midfoot for balance.
2. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning too far forward.
3. Push your knees out in line with your toes during each pulse.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the legs.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms crossed over your chest.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
3. Raise up a few cm, then lower back to the parallel position in a small pulse.
4. Keep pulsing in the lower range with control.
5. Stand back up to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and weight over your midfoot for balance.
2. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning too far forward.
3. Push your knees out in line with your toes during each pulse.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the legs.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips.
2. Step your right foot back and lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee is just above the ground.
3. Keep your front knee stacked over your ankle.
4. Push through your front heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat with the left foot stepping back, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
2. Lower your back knee straight down rather than reaching forward.
3. Drive through the front heel to stand up.
4. Move with control to keep your balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.
2. Step your right foot back and lower into a lunge while raising both arms straight in front to shoulder height.
3. Keep your front knee stacked over your ankle and your back knee just above the ground.
4. Push through your front heel to stand up while lowering your arms.
5. Repeat with the left foot stepping back, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Inhale as you lunge down and exhale as you stand up.
2. Keep your arms straight and stop the raise at shoulder height.
3. Keep your torso upright as you lower.
4. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.

instructions:
1. Stand on your right leg with a slight bend in the knee and your hands by your sides.
2. Hinge at the hip and lean your torso forward while lifting your left leg straight behind you.
3. Keep your back flat and lower until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your right heel and squeeze your glute to return to standing.
5. Finish the set, then switch to the left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and avoid twisting the torso.
2. Move slowly to stay balanced on the standing leg.
3. Fix your eyes on a point ahead to help with balance.
4. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
2. Extend your arms in front of you for balance.
3. Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your back straight and your heels flat.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
2. Keep your weight on your heels and midfoot.
3. Brace your core to keep your spine neutral.
4. Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms by your sides.
2. Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Push through your heels to stand back up.
4. Raise your right leg straight in front of you to hip level, then lower it.
5. Squat again, then raise your left leg straight in front to hip level and lower it.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes during the squat.
2. Keep your torso upright when raising the leg.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on the standing leg.
4. Move the raised leg slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms by your sides.
2. Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Push through your heels to stand back up.
4. Raise your right leg out to the side until straight, then lower it.
5. Squat again, then raise your left leg out to the side and lower it.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes during the squat.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning toward the raised leg.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on the standing leg.
4. Lift the side leg with control, not by swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms by your sides.
2. Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Push through your heels to stand back up, then raise your right leg out to the side and lower it.
4. Squat again, then stand up and raise your right leg straight to the front and lower it.
5. Switch sides and repeat the pattern with your left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes during the squat.
2. Keep your torso upright through both leg raises.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on the standing leg.
4. Move each leg raise slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
2. Extend your arms in front of you for balance.
3. Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your back straight and your heels flat.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
2. Keep your weight on your heels and midfoot.
3. Brace your core to keep your spine neutral.
4. Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and cross your arms over your chest.
2. Bend your knees and push your hips back to lower into a squat.
3. Stop when your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
4. Hold the position, keeping your chest up and weight on your heels.
5. Press through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
2. Keep your feet flat and weight on your heels.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso upright.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your back against a wall.
2. Extend your arms down at your sides, palms facing forward.
3. Sweep your arms out and up overhead in a wide arc, keeping them near the wall.
4. Bring your arms back down the same path to your sides.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the wall for alignment.
2. Move slowly and with control through the full arc.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop the arc where your shoulders feel comfortable.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Reach both arms behind your back and clasp your hands together.
3. Straighten your arms and lift your hands away from your back.
4. Gently arch your upper back and lift your chest toward the ceiling.
5. Hold the stretch, then return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move into the stretch slowly to protect your shoulders.
2. Keep the arch in your upper back, not your lower back.
3. Draw your shoulder blades down and together.
4. Breathe deeply and hold without bouncing.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, hands on your hips for balance.
2. Keep your legs straight and core engaged.
3. Push through the balls of your feet and lift your heels as high as you can.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower your heels back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rise as high onto your toes as possible for full range.
2. Lower slowly to keep tension on the calves.
3. Keep your knees straight to target the gastrocnemius.
4. Keep your weight even across both feet.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides, elbows bent to 90 degrees at shoulder height.
3. Squeeze your chest and bring your forearms together in front of your face.
4. Open your arms back out to the sides with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as your forearms meet.
2. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
3. Move slowly and with control in both directions.
4. Keep your elbows at shoulder height throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, upper arms parallel to the floor, elbows bent at 90 degrees and hands at shoulder height.
2. Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
3. Press your hands straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Lower your hands back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stop your lower back from arching.
2. Press in a straight line close to your head.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Set your upper arms parallel to the floor, elbows bent at 90 degrees, hands at shoulder height.
3. Press your hands straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Lower your hands back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head, upper back and hips in contact with the wall.
2. Press in a straight line along the wall.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands on your hips.
2. Keep your torso upright and arms relaxed.
3. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
4. Lower your shoulders back down under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift straight up and down, do not roll the shoulders.
2. Keep your chin level and neck relaxed.
3. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the traps.
4. Move slowly and with control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your upper arms to shoulder height with elbows bent, forming a triangle, elbows pointing out.
3. Sweep your elbows together in front of your chest.
4. Open your elbows back out to the sides under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as your elbows meet.
2. Keep your torso upright and ribs down.
3. Keep your neck relaxed, do not push your head forward.
4. Move slowly on the opening phase.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a step box, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place your right foot fully on the box.
3. Push through your right heel and bring your left foot up onto the box.
4. Step down with your left foot, then your right foot.
5. Repeat, alternating the lead foot.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the leading foot.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced for balance.
3. Place your whole foot on the box to avoid slipping.
4. Control the step down, do not drop.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and press your palms together in front of your chest, elbows bent.
2. Push your palms together hard to create tension in your chest.
3. Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your palms pressed together.
4. Bend your elbows to bring your hands back to your chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your palms together firmly the whole time to keep tension on the chest.
2. Keep your core tight to stay stable.
3. Move slowly and with control.
4. Breathe out as you extend your arms.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands on the floor at shoulder-width and arms straight, positioned slightly in front of your shoulders.
2. Keep your core tight and elbows tucked.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your forearms to the floor.
4. Press through your palms to straighten your arms and lift your forearms off the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Engage your core so your hips do not sag.
3. Keep elbows tucked close to your body to load the triceps.
4. Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press up.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back to a wall and feet shoulder-width apart, about 15 cm from the wall.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat until your buttocks touch the wall.
3. Push through your heels to stand back up.
4. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees in line with your toes.
2. Keep your core braced for stability.
3. Push through your heels, not your toes.
4. Move with control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Hinge at the hips and rotate your torso to touch your right hand to your left foot, keeping your left arm pointing up.
3. Return to standing.
4. Hinge and rotate the other way to touch your left hand to your right foot.
5. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to control the rotation.
2. Hinge from the hips rather than rounding your back.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
4. Move slowly and with control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Hinge at the hips and rotate your torso to touch your right hand toward your left foot, keeping your left arm pointing up.
3. Pulse the reach a few times at the bottom.
4. Return to standing, then hinge and rotate the other way to touch your left hand toward your right foot.
5. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to control the rotation and pulses.
2. Hinge from the hips rather than rounding your back.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
4. Keep the pulses small and controlled.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended just off the floor and arms by your sides.
2. Press your lower back into the floor and engage your core.
3. Bend your knees toward your chest until your thighs are vertical.
4. Lower your legs back down without letting them touch the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to protect your spine.
2. Move slowly and with control.
3. Drive the motion from your lower abs.
4. Breathe out as you bring your knees in.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Hold your hands in front of your hips.
3. Straighten your legs while drawing circles outward and upward with your hands.
4. Bend your knees as you circle your hands back down and inward to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and movements fluid.
3. Hold a steady rhythm with legs and arms.
4. Engage your core to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms out at shoulder level.
2. Rotate your torso and reach your left hand to the inside of your right thigh, bending your knees slightly.
3. Return to the start.
4. Rotate to the other side, reaching your right hand to the inside of your left thigh.
5. Continue alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your gaze forward to stay balanced.
2. Drive the rotation from your obliques, not your arms.
3. Move at a controlled pace.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in front of a box.
2. Bend your knees and hips and swing your arms back.
3. Swing your arms forward and jump explosively onto the box.
4. Land softly with both feet and knees bent.
5. Stand up fully, then step back down to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
2. Drive your arms up to add power.
3. Step down rather than jumping down to spare your joints.
4. Brace your core during takeoff and landing.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in front of a box.
2. Bend your knees and hips and swing your arms back.
3. Jump explosively onto the box and land softly in a squat.
4. Stand up, then jump or step back down to the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly in the squat with bent knees.
2. Keep your chest up as you land.
3. Drive your arms up to add power.
4. Brace your core throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up near your chin.
2. Snap your left arm straight forward, extending the elbow to throw the jab.
3. Turn the lead fist over so the palm faces down at full extension.
4. Quickly pull the left arm back to the guard position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the right hand up against your chin to protect your face.
2. Push off the lead foot to add power.
3. Exhale sharply as the punch lands.
4. Snap the punch and retract fast rather than pushing.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up near your chin.
2. Pivot on your left foot and rotate your hips and shoulders to the right.
3. Swing your left arm in a horizontal arc with the elbow bent about 90 degrees.
4. Quickly bring the left arm back to the guard position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the punch from your hip and torso rotation, not the arm.
2. Keep the right hand up to protect your face.
3. Keep the left elbow bent and level through the arc.
4. Exhale sharply as the punch lands.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up near your chin.
2. Dip slightly by bending your knees and dropping your left shoulder.
3. Drive up through your legs and rotate your hips as you bring the left fist upward in a rising arc.
4. Quickly bring the left arm back to the guard position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power by driving up from the legs and hips.
2. Keep the right hand up to protect your face.
3. Keep the punch compact and do not over-swing.
4. Exhale sharply as the punch rises.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up near your chin.
2. Pivot on your right foot and rotate your hips and shoulders forward.
3. Drive your right arm straight forward, extending the elbow to throw the cross.
4. Turn the rear fist over so the palm faces down at full extension.
5. Quickly pull the right arm back to the guard position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate the back foot and hips to drive power into the punch.
2. Keep the left hand up to protect your face.
3. Exhale sharply as the punch lands.
4. Push off the rear leg to extend through the target.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up near your chin.
2. Pivot on your right foot and rotate your hips and shoulders to the left.
3. Swing your right arm in a horizontal arc with the elbow bent about 90 degrees.
4. Quickly bring the right arm back to the guard position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the punch from your hip and torso rotation, not the arm.
2. Keep the left hand up to protect your face.
3. Keep the right elbow bent and level through the arc.
4. Exhale sharply as the punch lands.

instructions:
1. Stand in a boxing stance with feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, hands up near your chin.
2. Bend your knees slightly and load your right hip.
3. Drive up through your legs and rotate your hips and right shoulder.
4. Bring your right fist upward in a rising arc to throw the uppercut.
5. Quickly retract your right arm back to the guard position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your left hand up to protect your face.
2. Drive power from your legs and hips, not just your arm.
3. Exhale sharply as you throw the punch.
4. Keep your core braced to transfer force and stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank on your hands and toes, arms straight under your shoulders, body in a straight line.
2. Bend your right knee and drive it toward your left elbow, rotating your hips slightly.
3. Return your right leg to the plank position.
4. Bend your left knee and drive it toward your right elbow with a slight hip rotation.
5. Return to the plank position and keep alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips low and level, do not let them pike up.
2. Control each rep instead of rushing.
3. Exhale as the knee comes in, inhale as it returns.
4. Keep your shoulders stacked over your hands.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor at shoulder width, arms at your sides.
2. Lift your hips off the floor into a straight line from shoulders to knees.
3. Keep your hips elevated and press your knees outward in a controlled motion.
4. Bring your knees back together while keeping the hips up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips elevated and level the whole time.
2. Squeeze your glutes at the top of each rep.
3. Move your knees slowly and avoid jerking.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank on your hands and toes, body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Bend your right knee and drive it toward your left elbow, rotating your hips slightly.
3. Stop when your knee passes the elbow, then return to the plank.
4. Drive your left knee toward your right elbow with a slight hip rotation.
5. Return to the plank and keep alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your movements smooth and controlled.
2. Exhale as the knee drives in, inhale as it returns.
3. Keep your shoulders stable over your hands.
4. Brace your core to keep your hips from sagging.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, arms at your sides.
2. Press through your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
3. Straighten the front of your thighs and lift your chest.
4. Hold the position and breathe steadily.
5. Lower your hips back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees aligned over your ankles.
2. Squeeze your glutes and brace your core to support your lower back.
3. Keep your neck relaxed and avoid turning your head.
4. Breathe deeply and evenly throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and arms by your sides.
2. Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
3. Keep your hips level and extend your right leg straight, in line with your torso.
4. Lower the right leg without dropping your hips.
5. Extend your left leg straight, then lower it.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
2. Keep your hips level and do not let one side dip when a leg lifts.
3. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
4. Move the legs slowly and with control.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed by your sides.
2. Walk forward at a brisk pace with quick, short steps.
3. Land heel first and roll through to push off the toes.
4. Swing your arms naturally, opposite to your legs.
5. Keep your torso tall and core braced.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive off the toes of the back foot to power each step.
2. Keep your posture tall and shoulders relaxed.
3. Breathe steadily and rhythmically.
4. Keep your core gently braced for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed by your sides.
2. Walk at a brisk pace with quick, short steps.
3. Gradually turn as you walk to trace a full 360 degree circle.
4. Land heel first and push off the toes with each step.
5. Keep your torso tall and core braced as you turn.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lean slightly into the turn and keep steps even.
2. Use your hips to control direction, not your upper body.
3. Keep posture tall and shoulders relaxed.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, facing away from it.
2. Place the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
3. Set your right foot firmly on the floor in front of the bench.
4. Bend your right knee and hip to lower until your right thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your right heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Drive through the front heel to load the glute and quad.
3. Keep your torso slightly forward and core braced for balance.
4. Set the front foot far enough forward to keep the knee behind the toes.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, facing away from it.
2. Place the top of your right foot on the bench behind you.
3. Set your left foot firmly on the floor in front of the bench.
4. Bend your left knee and hip to lower until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your left heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Drive through the front heel to load the glute and quad.
3. Keep your torso slightly forward and core braced for balance.
4. Set the front foot far enough forward to keep the knee behind the toes.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, facing away from it.
2. Place the top of your left foot on the bench behind you. Keep your right foot flat on the floor.
3. Bend your right knee and hip to lower your body, keeping your torso upright, until your right thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your right heel to stand back up.
5. Finish the set, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Place most of your weight on the front foot, not the rear.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you drive up.
4. Move the front foot farther from the bench to shift load to the glutes.

instructions:
1. Stand in front of a bench, facing away from it. Place the band under your front foot.
2. Set the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you.
3. Hold the band handles near your shoulders with palms facing forward.
4. Bend your front knee to lower your body until your back knee is just above the floor.
5. Drive through your front heel to stand back up, then switch legs after the set.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
2. Track your front knee over your toes.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep tension on the band so it stays under the front foot.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms at your sides.
2. Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
3. Jump your feet back into a plank, keeping your body in a straight line.
4. Lower into a push-up, then push back up.
5. Jump your feet back to your hands, then jump straight up with arms overhead.
6. Land softly, drop back into the squat, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level in the plank, do not let them sag.
2. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
3. Brace your core through every transition.
4. Set a steady pace you can hold with good form.
name: Burpee

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
2. Lower into a squat and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
3. Jump or step both feet back into a plank, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
4. Jump or step both feet back to the squat position.
5. Stand tall to finish the rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced in the plank so your hips do not sag.
2. Land softly on the balls of your feet to protect your knees.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes during the squat.
4. Exhale as you stand up.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms reaching forward, palms down.
2. Bend your right knee to bring your heel toward your buttocks.
3. At the same time, pull both elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
4. Return to the start and switch to the left leg.
5. Keep alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest tall and avoid leaning forward.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
3. Drive each heel high to fully engage the hamstrings.
4. Exhale as you pull your elbows back.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Jog in place, kicking your right heel up toward your buttocks.
3. Switch quickly, kicking your left heel up toward your buttocks.
4. Keep your knees pointing down and swing your arms naturally.
5. Continue alternating heels at a quick pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
2. Brace your core for balance and stability.
3. Use quick, light foot contacts to fire the hamstrings.
4. Stay on the balls of your feet.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Slowly lift your right heel up toward your buttocks.
3. Lower it and slowly lift your left heel toward your buttocks.
4. Keep your knees pointing down and your movements controlled.
5. Continue alternating heels at a steady, slow pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
2. Brace your core for balance and stability.
3. Control each heel lift to feel the hamstrings work.
4. Move with control rather than speed.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet pressed together and your knees out to the sides.
2. Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall.
3. Gently lower both knees toward the floor.
4. Raise both knees back up in a smooth flapping motion.
5. Continue the controlled up and down motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid slouching.
2. Breathe steadily and evenly throughout.
3. Use gentle, controlled motion to protect the hip joints.
4. Do not force the knees down past a comfortable range.
